pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/sandbox.rs:721 A sandbox session from an earlier daemon process that has no session.json is reported as Failed. A session killed mid-run looks exactly like that, and so does a session that really failed (which leaves error.json, a file this code never reads), so an outcome nobody knows is recorded as a known failure.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/sandbox.rs:705 When a later daemon recovers a session, it gets only Done or Failed. A run that was interrupted is closed as Failed, not as indeterminate (see line 721, and the test at line 1339 that pins this).

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/casework.rs:1454 The egress policy reaches the Researcher as CLI WebFetch rules, not as a file it can write. The pipeline then checks each URL the model proposed against the allowlist again before fetching it, so an escape is caught by the pipeline's own fetcher.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/casework.rs:749 Loose analogy: the pipeline's own fetch falls back to a Wayback capture. The text the model reads says the page was substituted and names the capture, and the stored record keeps `via`. Caveat: `retrieved` is the day the page was served; the time it was obtained is only in the capture URL.

pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-types/src/sandbox.rs:81 The sandbox session status vocabulary is Running, Closing, Judging, Done, Failed and Stopped. There is no indeterminate status, so a consumer that finds an interrupted session can only call it Failed (which the daemon does).

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-types/src/sandbox.rs:81 The technique says that when the vocabulary lacks an indeterminate status, you add one. This shared contract enum has none.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/engine.rs:115 EngineReply names the producer that actually answered (engine, account, model) and gives fallback_reason when a fallback served the call.
